reflections.title: "The LORD Stirred the Spirit of Cyrus"

reflect.text: Long before Cyrus ruled Persia, God had already promised through the prophet Jeremiah that the exile would end after seventy years. When that time came, the sovereign God stirred the heart of this foreign king. Cyrus made God's work a top priority by allowing the exiles to return and rebuild the temple. God is completely free to work through anyone He chooses to carry out His plans, even rulers who do not know Him. Recognizing that God is using an unbelieving leader does not mean we must approve of everything that person does.

God remains the true source of every great spiritual movement. F. B. Meyer observed that in prayer we can "touch the spring of all the stirrings that the world needs." When Daniel realized God's promised time was near, he gave himself to prayer. God still speaks to human hearts today, calling people to faith and directing believers to serve Him. When God moves in our lives through His Word and prayer, we must stay sensitive to His Holy Spirit and be willing to obey.

questions: How does knowing that God directs world leaders give you peace when world events feel uncertain?
In what ways can you stay sensitive and obedient to the Holy Spirit's promptings in your daily life?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for Your sovereignty over all nations and earthly rulers. Soften the hearts of leaders to accomplish Your good purposes in our world. Keep our hearts sensitive to Your Holy Spirit during prayer and Bible study, so that we may quickly obey whenever You call us to serve. In Jesus' name, Amen.
